title: SEC-8b.7 — replace dangling ISS-2046 'is tracked as' reference with completion-record summary
scope: Update the closing paragraph of SEC-8b.7 (data/sections.json part8b html) so the lingering 'is tracked as ISS-2046' clause reflects that ISS-2046 was closed on 2026-05-17 with resolution 'Citation compliance audit complete: 45 dome URLs in sections.json. 38 formally compliant, 7 documented exceptions. No patches needed.' Without this update, the reader following the dated-record/audit-hook standard the section is itself making is sent to an issue that the project has already retired. Single-paragraph string_replace; verdict and surrounding structure unchanged. Mode 6 read-only-surfacing path: this EXP proposes the change for the decider to integrate, not in-line remediation.

mode6_finding.finding_summary: ISS-2046 (severity minor, category missing_argument) was filed by EXP-399 / SEC-8b.c1-hole-2 on 2026-05-17 to track a citation-compliance audit of pre-2026-04-18 references in data/sections.json. It was closed the same day by analyst-baby EXP-398 with resolution 'Citation compliance audit complete: 45 dome URLs in sections.json. 38 formally compliant, 7 documented exceptions. No patches needed.' (monitor/decisions/closed-issues.json). The closing paragraph of SEC-8b.7, however, still narrates the audit in present-tense-pending form: 'A retrospective audit of pre-2026-04-18 citations — to bring legacy references into the same compliance and flag any that conflict with currently-served dome content — is tracked as ISS-2046.' A reader applying the section's own standard (paragraph 1: 'every citation carries an explicit "as of [date]" label'; paragraph 3 of 8b.7: 'whether our prose consistently meets that bar is an empirical question … the audit hooks in paragraph 2 are what would make the answer checkable') is sent to a closed issue presented as open. This is the exact failure mode the surrounding paragraphs commit not to commit. Mode 6 is the dispatcher's fresh-eyes pass; this is the kind of post-integration drift it is designed to catch. The integrity agent's deterministic checks do not catch it because the cross-reference is a project-internal token, not a URL or DOM anchor; the broken-cross-ref scan looks for hash anchors that fail to resolve, not for ISS tokens whose status has flipped to closed.
mode6_finding.cross_ref_audit_run: Examined SEC-8b.7 in full. Confirmed: (1) all hash anchors referenced in part8b html either resolve to ids present in sections.json or are generated by build-scripts/generate-html.js (timestamp tab at line 1928; pred-pred-095 generated by the pred.id.toLowerCase().replace pattern at line 1020/1099). (2) Cited monitor/changes/chg-20260417-1620-001.json through -005.json all exist on disk (and -006.json also exists, harmless — section cites 001-005 specifically). (3) Section 4.6 'Registry Framing Audit' cross-reference resolves textually (part4 mentions it) — no hash anchor needed for that style of citation. (4) Dome-side commit SHAs 5021eec and 6e06efb are dome-repo SHAs and not verifiable from our repo, but consistent with the dated change-archive records. (5) ISS-2046 — flipped to closed 2026-05-17 — is the only drifted reference. Single-finding output.
mode6_finding.why_this_is_a_real_issue: The section's load-bearing commitment is dated-record consistency. SEC-8b.7 §4 commits: 'failed predictions stay failed. A registered prediction … that misses its target is recorded as a miss and remains so … Symmetric rules are auditable.' Symmetric rules cut both ways: a closed audit hook that the prose narrates as open is the same class of error as a failed prediction re-described as pending. Leaving the dangling reference would make the section's own standard inapplicable to itself. The fix is small (one string_replace) and the change preserves the dated-record commitment by adding the closure date and the audit's quantitative result to the prose. It does not retire the underlying commitment ('Future references on this section that fall out of compliance can be filed as new issues') because the section's standing rule remains in force — only the single tracked instance has resolved.
mode6_finding.not_a_remediation: Per the Mode 6 read-only-surfacing rule (analyst.md 'Mode 6 is READ-ONLY surfacing — DO NOT remediate in-line'), this EXP does NOT mutate data/sections.json, monitor/decisions/closed-issues.json, or any other state file directly. The patch is proposed for decider integration via the normal EXP → decider pipeline. No tracker entry is mutated by Mode 6 itself (matching the convention used by EXP-627 and EXP-628; the decider integrates Mode 6 EXPs from the expansion-file scan).

analyst_assessment: The replacement carries the closure date, the audit's quantitative finding (45 URLs / 38 compliant / 7 exceptions), and an explicit forward-looking clause ('the standing commitment carries forward and is not retired') so the section's commitment is not weakened by recording the single resolution. The two-axis cross-check the section asks the reader to apply (current-wording + dated-record) is preserved; only the present-tense framing of an already-completed audit is corrected. Verdict, tab placement, surrounding paragraphs, and hash anchors are unchanged.
kernel_of_truth: The original prose was right to flag the audit and to commit to tracking it — that's the section's epistemic discipline working as intended. The failure mode is purely temporal: the prose was written when the audit was open, and was not refreshed when the audit closed. This is not a content error, it is an integration-drift error. The replacement preserves the original commitment intact (the standing rule that future non-compliance gets filed as new issues) and only corrects the present-tense narration of a completed instance.

anticipated_objections.objection: The new prose is longer; does the section need a six-sentence audit-history block where it had one closing sentence?
anticipated_objections.response: The original sentence carried weight beyond its length — it was the load-bearing audit-hook that paragraph 3 of 8b.7 named as the empirical check on the section's own dated-record claim. Replacing it with a one-clause 'audit complete' phrase would erase the empirical-check structure. The replacement adds two facts (the closure date, the audit numbers) and one forward-looking clause (the standing commitment doesn't retire) — three additions in service of preserving the same empirical-check structure. Net characters grow ~47%; net signal grows proportionally.

anticipated_objections.objection: Why not delete the dangling reference entirely instead of replacing it?
anticipated_objections.response: Deleting it would remove the section's most visible empirical check (paragraph 3 of 8b.7 explicitly names the audit hooks of paragraph 2 as 'what would make the answer checkable'). The dated-record commitment is strengthened by recording the resolution, not by erasing the trace. This is the same dated-history-is-evidence discipline the section applies to dome-side WIN-058's path from confirmed to pending — symmetrically applied to ourselves.

anticipated_objections.objection: Could the closure record itself be wrong? analyst-baby is Sonnet, not Opus — should an Opus review of EXP-398 (the audit that closed ISS-2046) happen first?
anticipated_objections.response: The closure resolution is mechanical: 45 URLs walked, 38 carry explicit dates, 7 are accepted as exceptions. The work is auditable from data/sections.json itself. The Mode 6 finding here is independent of whether EXP-398's numbers are precisely right — even if the precise count later shifts (e.g., a re-audit finds 44 instead of 45), the dangling 'is tracked as' clause remains the integration-drift bug. If the underlying audit needs revisiting, a separate EXP can be queued and the prose updated again — preserving the dated-history pattern. The current EXP fixes the integration-drift; subsequent updates to the audit numbers would be separate work.

anticipated_objections.objection: What about other closed-issue references in other sections — should a sweep be run?
anticipated_objections.response: The c3-style anti-sweep guidance applies here: each section's references should be evaluated on their own merits. Mode 6 is designed to surface one fresh-eyes finding per run; a mechanical sweep across all sections for closed-issue references would be a separate, tinker-class refactor proposal, not analyst Mode 6 work. The current EXP is scoped to SEC-8b.7 only. If the operator wants a sweep, that's an HNOTE/proposal-class task — not the Mode 6 random-look path.
